name: narrow_range_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, when any 5-second bar has the narrowest high-low range of the preceding 7 bars (~35 seconds), institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms have reached momentary equilibrium — neither side is absorbing aggressively. This NR7 bar coils resting limit orders at its high and low. The first subsequent 5-second bar that closes above the NR7 high signals buy-side flow has overwhelmed the resting supply ceiling, triggering momentum algos and delta-hedging rebalances that extend the move 15-25 NIFTY spot points over the next 30-60 seconds. Trading only when the NR7 bar sits above/below EMA(60) filters against counter-trend fakeouts, which dominate when the 5-minute trend is directional and NR bars form against the grain.

indicators.name: bar_range
indicators.purpose: Per-bar high-low range — the raw input to the NR7 condition.

indicators.name: is_nr7
indicators.purpose: 7-bar lookback preserved from the original (NOT 12x-scaled). NR7 is a relative measure — 'is this bar narrower than the previous 6?' — which does not depend on bar duration. At 5s, 7 bars = 35 seconds of micro-consolidation, exactly the right coiling window before a 15-60 second breakout hold. Scaling to 84 bars (7 minutes) would detect session-scale consolidation, far too slow for our entry timing.

indicators.name: ema_60
indicators.purpose: 5-minute EMA as trend context. The original used EMA(20) on 1-min bars = 20-minute EMA. Compressed to 5 minutes (60 bars × 5s) because we hold 15-60 seconds — at that hold horizon, the relevant question is whether the 5-minute trend supports the breakout direction, not the 20-minute trend. A 20-minute EMA (240 bars) would be too slow to react to intraday regime shifts at our holding time.

conditions: is_nr7[i-1] == True  (previous bar was the narrowest of its 7-bar window)
close[i] > high[i-1]  (current bar closes above the NR7 bar's high — confirmed upside breakout)
close[i-1] > ema_60[i-1]  (NR7 bar formed in 5-minute uptrend context)
buy_ce.confirmation: Single 5-second bar close above NR7 bar high — no multi-bar confirmation needed because 5s resolution allows us to enter on the first breakout bar rather than waiting.

conditions: is_nr7[i-1] == True  (previous bar was the narrowest of its 7-bar window)
close[i] < low[i-1]  (current bar closes below the NR7 bar's low — confirmed downside breakout)
close[i-1] < ema_60[i-1]  (NR7 bar formed in 5-minute downtrend context)
buy_pe.confirmation: Single 5-second bar close below NR7 bar low — same rationale as buy_ce.

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta ~0.5. An NR7 breakout that reverses 8 spot points back below the NR7 bar's high has definitively failed — genuine coil breakouts on NIFTY do not immediately retrace more than the NR7 range itself (which at 5s resolution is typically 3-8 spot points). This gives a 1:1.75 risk-reward at the 7-pt target.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points. The original targeted 2x the NR7 bar range. On NIFTY at 5-second resolution, a genuine NR7 breakout extension (momentum algos and delta-hedgers piling in) typically extends 15-25 spot points in the first 30-60 seconds. 7 pts captures the lower end of this range, consistent with our 60-second time stop (1-min typical move: 3-7 option pts).

filters.vix_filter: none — NR7 breakouts are regime-independent; tight coils form in both low- and high-vol environments
filters.time_filter: 09:20-15:25 IST — skip pre-open noise; EMA(60) needs 5 min warmup
filters.volume_filter: none — NIFTY 5-second volume is too noisy; the NR7 price condition is sufficient
filters.trend_filter: EMA(60) direction — NR7 bar must sit above EMA for CE, below EMA for PE
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at candle close prices

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volatility clustering is a structural market property; NR7 at 5s is underexplored on NIFTY

adaptation_notes: Key changes from original (Strategy_34.json): (1) Universe changed from top-30 FnO stocks to NIFTY index — smoother, institutional-driven, no single-stock gaps. (2) NR7 lookback kept at 7 bars (not 12x scaled) — the relative-narrowness criterion is bar-size agnostic; 35 seconds of coiling is appropriate for a 15-60s hold. (3) EMA compressed from 20-min (EMA_20 on 1-min) to 5-min (EMA_60 on 5s) to match hold time horizon. (4) ATR declining filter DROPPED — at 5-second resolution, the NR7 condition itself is the volatility contraction signal; adding ATR would double-count. (5) Volume confirmation on breakout bar DROPPED — NIFTY 5s volume is extremely noisy; close above NR7 high is a cleaner signal. (6) Stop/target converted from percentage-of-NR7-range to fixed option premium points calibrated to typical 30-60s NIFTY move magnitudes.
weaknesses: NR7 at 5-second resolution fires frequently (10-20x per session) — many signals during low-liquidity mid-session (12:00-13:00) are fakeouts
Single-bar coil (35 seconds) is short enough that a single large institutional print can create a false NR7 followed by immediate reversal
EMA(60) lags in choppy sessions — trend flips every few minutes, reducing the quality of the trend filter

_source.original_stop: opposite end of NR7 bar (full NR7 range as risk)
